angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,196,604 km at 87.65 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.4090 +/- 0.0259 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 87.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.72 +/- 0.041 solar radii from Bieryla et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4641 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.52710955B/abstract): 1,196,604 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.41 +/- 0.068 solar masses from Bieryla et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4641 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.52710955B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6560 +/- 300 K from Bieryla et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4641 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.52710955B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bieryla et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4641 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.52710955B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4641.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.116, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
